verses.text: David was told, "Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and are stealing the grain from the threshing floors."
So David asked the LORD, "Shall I go and attack these Philistines?" The LORD answered him, "Go, attack the Philistines and save Keilah."
But David's men said to him, "Even here in Judah we are afraid. How much more if we go to Keilah against the Philistine army!"
Once again David asked the LORD, and the LORD answered him, "Go down to Keilah, because I am going to give the Philistines into your hands."
So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He carried off their animals and struck them down badly. So David saved the people of Keilah.
When Abiathar son of Ahimelek had run to David at Keilah, he had brought the ephod down with him.
Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, and he said, "God has handed him over to me, because David has trapped himself by going into a town with gates and bars."
So Saul called up all his forces for battle, to go down to Keilah and surround David and his men.
When David learned that Saul was planning evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod."
David said, "LORD, God of Israel, your servant has heard for certain that Saul plans to come to Keilah and destroy the town because of me.
Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, please tell your servant." And the LORD said, "He will come down."
Again David asked, "Will the leaders of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?" And the LORD said, "They will."
So David and his men, about six hundred in number, left Keilah and kept moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he did not go there.
David stayed in the desert strongholds and in the hills of the Desert of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God did not give David into his hands.
While David was at Horesh in the Desert of Ziph, he learned that Saul had come out to kill him.
And Saul's son Jonathan went to David at Horesh and helped him find strength in God.
"Do not be afraid," he said. "My father Saul will not lay a hand on you. You will be king over Israel, and I will be second to you. Even my father Saul knows this."
The two of them made a covenant before the LORD. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh.
The Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is David not hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hakilah, south of Jeshimon?
Now, Your Majesty, come down whenever it pleases you, and we will be responsible for handing him over to the king."
Saul replied, "The LORD bless you for your kindness to me.
Go and get more information. Find out where David usually goes and who has seen him there. I am told he is very cunning.
Find out about all the hiding places he uses, and come back to me with sure information. Then I will go with you. If he is in the area, I will track him down among all the clans of Judah."
So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. But David and his men were in the Desert of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.
Saul and his men began the search. When David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Desert of Maon. When Saul heard this, he went into the Desert of Maon chasing David.

Saul was going along one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other side, hurrying to get away from Saul. As Saul and his forces were closing in on David and his men to capture them,
a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Come quickly! The Philistines are raiding the land."
Then Saul stopped chasing David and went to fight the Philistines. That is why they call this place Sela Hammahlekoth, which means Rock of Parting.
And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.
